description:
We're SynthMinds, a group of people who love exploring ideas, figuring things out, and building things that once seemed impossible. We're joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge because we see it as more than a competition it's a chance to learn from others, challenge ourselves, and work on problems bigger than our everyday world.
We're interested in AI, technology, science, and the endless possibilities that come when different minds work together.
summary:
We developed an interactive Mars mission trainer built around the 2018 Mars global dust storm. Using real NASA data, it visualizes how the storm spreads across the planet’s surface. Players then step into the role of an astronaut inside a habitat dome and watch the storm’s impact unfold: as dust blocks sunlight, solar power drops and battery reserves shrink.

The trainer addresses the challenge by turning real science into hands-on learning. Instead of reading about Mars hazards, junior astronauts experience them and make choice-based decisions, such as which systems to prioritize or how to ration limited power, while protecting essential life support.

This matters because future Mars missions will depend on astronauts who can monitor environmental conditions and manage scarce resources under pressure. By combining real NASA data with decision-making gameplay, our project builds critical thinking, awareness of Martian hazards, and survival skills in an engaging way that inspires the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Mars is a dusty planet. Wind often lifts dust from the surface in to the air forming clouds of dust at different locations across Mars. These dust storms typically last up to a couple days and grow to a few hundred km in size. This project is built around the 2018 Mars global dust storm and visualizes what happens when the storm sweeps across the planet's surface using the real time NASA’s Data . It also shows how an astronaut inside a dom reacts as the storm hits.

As the dust blocks out sunlight, the power start shrinking, and the player is given choice-based options. The experience presents challenges associated with maintaining a habitat under hazardous environmental conditions, including reduced sunlight, atmospheric dust, limited battery power, and the need to preserve essential life-support systems.

The primary objective is to demonstrate how monitoring conditions and making resource-management decisions can help astronauts survive extreme environmental conditions on Mars.

The experience begins with the start screen, where the program loads its 3D models, sounds, and data. After loading, a guided tour takes the player across the Martian landscape, passing the rover and the small helicopter before entering the base. As the storm builds, real daily measurements from Mars are replayed one Martian day at a time, causing the sky to darken, the atmosphere to fill with dust, and the lighting to turn orange-brown. When the dust reaches dangerous levels, an emergency alarm sounds, red lights flash, and warning messages and live measurements appear on the screens. The player then gets 15 seconds to calmly look around and read the guide before the actual decision begins. At this stage, the base goes dark, oxygen levels start falling, and a 45-second countdown begins. The player must choose one of five available options, each accompanied by a short explanation. Finally, the consequences of the decision are shown: either the astronaut is successfully saved, or the mission fails. A summary card then explains the outcome and the reasons behind it.

The player can interact with the experience using simple keyboard and mouse controls. Moving the mouse allows the player to look around the Martian environment. The number keys 1, 2, and 3 can be used to turn and focus on the left, centre, or right screen, respectively. Pressing F allows the player to enter or exit full-screen mode, while pressing M mutes or unmutes the sound. These controls make it easy for the player to explore the environment and interact with the simulation.
